subject.title: [优化建议] 添加结构化错误处理和智能重试机制

question: What cross-platform npm installer failure policy should OpenClaw ship for retries, automatic repair, and fail-closed behavior?
rationale: The request spans first-run UX, retry behavior, optional setup probes, permission repair, and TLS/security-sensitive npm failures, so automation should not choose retry or remediation semantics without maintainer intent.

options.title: Conservative diagnostics and transient retries
options.body: Add structured error extraction and remediation text while retrying only clearly transient network errors and leaving certificate/security and persistent local failures explicit.

options.title: Broader automatic repair
options.body: Attempt safe permission or prefix repairs after EACCES-style failures and retry only when the platform-specific repair succeeds with tests and rollback behavior.

options.title: Diagnostics-only first
options.body: Keep install execution behavior mostly unchanged while improving error messages and docs, then revisit retries after more live failures are confirmed.

recommendation.title: Conservative diagnostics and transient retries
recommendation.body: Add structured error extraction and remediation text while retrying only clearly transient network errors and leaving certificate/security and persistent local failures explicit.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history points to vincentkoc as the strongest owner for installer/setup behavior across POSIX, Windows, and local-prefix paths.
